title: Measure is derived from the integral, and its two bounds hold in every integration space
statement: The measure of a set is DEFINED as the integral of its indicator, where that indicator is integrable: `IntSpace.measure S chi h := S.integral chi h`, with h the set-indexed integrability datum. There is no sigma-algebra, no measurable-set predicate and no measure as primitive data anywhere in the development. The two bounds a measure must satisfy are then theorems rather than axioms: `0 <= mu(A)` and `mu(A) <= mu(whole space)`, each from the generic monotonicity of the integral. `IntSpace.Indicator S chi` is the LOCATED condition `0 <= chi <= 1`, deliberately not idempotence `chi*chi ~ chi`: over the constructive reals a vanishing product does not decide which factor vanished, so idempotence does not deliver a two-valued function and would claim more than it gives. Because the integrability datum lives in Sort 1 (CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn is a Type whose modulus the integral consumes) and this kernel has no Sigma or Subtype, an integrable set is carried as a datum plus a Prop side condition rather than bundled into one object; the measured cost is one extra binder per theorem. A third theorem, `measure_witness_independent`, is what makes `the measure of the set` well defined at all: the value does not depend on WHICH integrability datum witnesses it. On a classical development that is not even a statement.

formal.statement: theorem IntSpace.measure_nonneg : ((x0 : IntSpace) -> ((x1 : IntSpace.carrier x0) -> ((x2 : IntSpace.Integrable x0 x1) -> ((x3 : IntSpace.Indicator x0 x1) -> CReal.le CReal.zero (IntSpace.measure x0 x1 x2)))))

evidence.supports: The measure layer -- measure, Indicator, measure_nonneg, measure_le_total, measure_witness_independent, measure_const, indicator_univ, measure_univ -- is admitted with empty axiom footprints.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib intspace::intspace_tests::every_intspace_declaration_is_axiom_free 2>&1) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 passed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The declaration list is derived from the IntSpacePrelude handle, so the sweep cannot silently omit a member of the measure layer.

evidence.supports: The definitional claim is checked rather than described: a Check theorem whose type is `Equiv (measure S chi h) (S.integral chi h)` at SYMBOLIC S, chi and h is admitted by CReal.Equiv.refl, so `measure` unfolds to the integral and to nothing else.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib intspace::intspace_tests::measure_unfolds_to_the_integral 2>&1) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 passed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Stated on symbolic arguments deliberately. A concrete-numeral probe on CReal is vacuous because numerals compute, so it would pass whatever the definition said.

evidence.supports: The direction of the bound is load-bearing: `0 <= integral f` is admitted and the REVERSED conclusion `integral f <= 0` from the same proof term is REFUSED, both in one test.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib intspace::intspace_tests::integral_nonneg_direction_is_load_bearing 2>&1) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 passed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: measure_nonneg is integral_nonneg composed with And.left, so the control on integral_nonneg's direction is the control on this fact's direction.

evidence.supports: The measure layer is not vacuous: EVERY detachable subset of a finite index set (a Nat -> Bool) is an integrable set of IntSpace.crealFinite, with IntSpace.Triv.mk as its datum, and the Dirac measure of one computes by CReal.Equiv.refl. Without this the Indicator predicate could have been satisfied only by constants.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib intspace::intspace_tests::bool_indicator_evaluates_and_the_crossed_pairing_is_refused 2>&1) && test "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 passed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The evaluation test checks BOTH branches of boolIndicator AND both crossed pairings in one test, so it cannot pass vacuously through a branch that always returns the same value.

provenance.established_by: axeyum-lean-kernel intspace::measure and intspace::detachable modules (integration-space lane, roadmap W3-1)
provenance.source: Derived from the IntSpace record's integralLe and integralConst fields. Design, and the predicativity constraint it is built under, in docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1612-the-integral-is-primitive-and-measure-is-derived-predicatively.md.

notes: WHY THIS FACT EXISTS. W3-1 (measure and the Lebesgue integral) is the department's largest shelf and reviewers 03 and 08 are blocked behind it. This is the inversion that shelf is being built on: measure is derived, not primitive. The honest boundary is recorded in ADR-1612 and not here: the integrable sets of the INTERVAL instance are trivial, because an integrable set there needs a uniformly continuous indicator and a uniformly continuous two-valued function on a connected interval is constant. The non-trivial content lives on the finite and Dirac instances until L1 -- the completion -- exists, and the two things blocking that completion are measured in the ADR (Sigma/Subtype, and a generic metric-completion construction).
